title: The Matthew Effect
coreMove: Accumulative advantage begins as a small head start, then grows when institutions hand the early winners more coaching, time, attention, and belief.

exampleSpecs.stakes: late-born players may lose elite coaching for a full season
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the Medicine Hat Tigers roster to question an early hockey selection decision.

exampleSpecs.audience: school leaders using one test score
exampleSpecs.stakes: younger students may be tracked away from richer instruction
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use fourth-grade standardized test gaps to audit gifted placement.

exampleSpecs.stakes: smaller children may leave the pipeline before growth catches up
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Apply the January 1 cutoff lesson to a soccer academy.

exampleSpecs.stakes: students with early exposure may monopolize the best mentor hours
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Translate accumulative advantage into mentor scheduling.

exampleSpecs.stakes: a young child may be labeled delayed from cohort timing alone
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use cohort timing to interpret a child readiness review.

exampleSpecs.stakes: older beginners may receive the lessons that create future advantage
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use the Matthew Effect to distribute music coaching.
